passages.text: ### 7.1 Error estimates at a fixed cutoff Fix the minimizer first and then $T<1$. The bounds below have constants depending on that minimizer and strip; they give an $N^{-1/2}$ rate there, not a rate uniform as $T\uparrow1$. Those derivative bounds are finite but have not been supplied as numerical inputs to an algorithm for choosing a mesh. The calculation is an ordinary deduction from the source's strip estimates, beyond the qualitative selected formal statement. Write $S_{T,N}=\sum_{j=0}^N A_jB_{j+1}$ and $f(t)=\mathbb E a(t,X_t)$, so $0\le f(t)\le1$. On the fixed strip let $K_T=\sup_{t\le T,x}|a(t,x)|$ and choose a spatial Lipschitz constant $L_T$ for $a$. Define $$ \delta_N=\max_{0\le j\le N}\|Y_j-X_{t_j}\|_2,\qquad d_N=\max_{1\le j\le N} \left|\mathbb E a(t_{j-1},Y_{j-1})^2-1\right|. $$ These errors have a rate at each fixed strip, even if $\gamma$ has jumps. Put $\Gamma=\gamma(T)$ and $V=\gamma(T)-\gamma(0)$. Bounded spatial derivatives and the PDE give temporal Lipschitz constants $$ J=\tfrac12\|u_{xx}\|_\infty+\Gamma K_T,\qquad H=\tfrac12\|a_{xx}\|_\infty+\Gamma(K_T^2+L_T) $$ for $u$ and $a$, respectively, on this strip. No derivative of $\gamma$ is used. Brownian coupling gives $\|X_s-X_{\pi_N(s)}\|_2\le\sqrt\Delta+\Gamma\Delta$. Subtract the Euler and diffusion equations and split the drift difference on $[t_j,t_{j+1}]$ as $$ \gamma(s)\bigl(u(s,X_s)-u(t_j,Y_j)\bigr) +\bigl(\gamma(s)-\gamma(t_j)\bigr)u(t_j,Y_j). $$ Put $A_T=\int_0^T\gamma(s)\,ds\le1$ and $w_j=\int_{t_j}^{t_{j+1}}\gamma(s)\,ds$. Taking a pathwise maximum over grid times, Minkowski and discrete Gronwall give, with $$ R_N=A_TK_T\sqrt\Delta+ [A_T(J+\Gamma K_T)+V]\Delta, $$ the bound $$ \delta_N\le\left\|\max_{j\le N}|Y_j-X_{t_j}|\right\|_2 \le e^{K_TA_T}R_N\le e^{K_T}R_N. $$ The recurrence weights the preceding maximal norm on interval $j$ by $K_Tw_j$; their sum is $K_TA_T$. The term $V\Delta$ is the monotone quadrature bound for the coefficient. For the martingale residual, Itô isometry and the same increment estimate give $$ e_N\le K_T\delta_N+ \sqrt T\{L_T\delta_N+L_T\sqrt\Delta+(H+\Gamma L_T)\Delta\}. $$ Thus $\delta_N,e_N=O_{\gamma,T}(\sqrt\Delta)$. These are deductions from the compact-strip bounds and stochastic identities, not quantitative clauses of the selected Lean statement. Since $a$ is bounded and Lipschitz, $d_N\le2K_TL_T\delta_N\to0$. Whenever $d_N\le1/2$, $$ \sqrt{2/3}\le c_j\le\sqrt2,\qquad |1/c_j-1|\le d_N,\qquad \|\alpha\|_2\le\sqrt{T(1+d_N)}. $$ These estimates give an explicit sufficient condition for all the required normalisers to be positive. They do not assume positivity for every coarse mesh. The first-moment identity in §6 makes $f=m$ nonincreasing, with $f(0)=1$. Its right Riemann sum therefore satisfies $$ 0\le I(T)-\Delta\sum_{j=1}^N f(t_j) \le\Delta\bigl(f(0)-f(T)\bigr). $$ Removing the last term adds $\Delta f(T)$, so $0\le I(T)-\Delta\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}f(t_j)\le\Delta$. The difference between the shifted interior sum and the integral is bounded by $$ \left|\Delta\sum_{j=1}^{N-1} \frac{\mathbb E a(t_j,Y_j)}{c_j}-\int_0^T f(t)\,dt\right| \le TK_Td_N+TL_T\delta_N+\Delta. $$ The first two terms replace the normalisers and Euler positions; the last is the preceding monotone quadrature estimate. Combining this with the vector and rounding-endpoint estimate gives $$ \begin{aligned} |S_{T,N}-P_*| \le{}&(1-T)m(T) +\bigl(2+\sqrt{T(1+d_N)}\bigr)e_N +\sqrt{\Delta(1+d_N)}\\ &+TK_Td_N+TL_T\delta_N+\Delta . \end{aligned} $$ In particular, for each fixed minimizer and $T<1$ there are finite $C_{\gamma,T}$ and $N_0(\gamma,T)$ such that $$ |S_{T,N}-P_*|\le(1-T)m(T)+C_{\gamma,T}\sqrt{T/N} \qquad(N\ge N_0(\gamma,T)). $$ The constants are not uniform as $T\uparrow1$. The [coefficient budget](#coefficient-budget) bounds $\int\gamma$ and $\gamma$ on each fixed strip, but numerical bounds for all strip derivative constants and an effective mesh threshold are not supplied. The scalar tail bound $(1-T)m(T)\le1-T$ uses only monotonicity of the first moment; Proposition 6.2 further makes it $o(1-T)$. All terms after this scalar tail tend to zero at each fixed $T<1$. Given a scalar tolerance $\zeta>0$, first choose $T$ with $1-T<\zeta/2$, then choose $N_0(\gamma,T,\zeta)$ so that their sum is below $\zeta/2$ for every $N\ge N_0$. This is the required finite choice of a Gaussian spin. The formula exposes the errors; it does not supply numerical values of $K_T,L_T,\delta_N,e_N$ or an effective mesh threshold. [OpenAI (2026a), Lemma 2.1][fs-reg]; [OpenAI (2026a), Proposition 7.2][fs-cons]. A diagonal can be chosen using these thresholds. For prescribed $T_m\uparrow1$, choose increasing $N_m$ large enough to make the mesh-dependent part of the fixed-$T_m$ bound less than $1/m$. An arbitrary increasing mesh schedule does not follow from the iterated limit alone. For example, the scalar array $$ h(T,N)=\min\{1,[N(1-T)]^{-1}\} $$ tends to zero in $N$ at every fixed $T<1$, but $h(1-1/N,N)=1$ for every $N\ge2$. This is an illustration of the quantifier issue, not an asserted error law for the SK construction.
